↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 37:21.

For grace is not given, him from the Lord, because he is deprived of all wisdom.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 37:22.

Another is wise to himself; and the fruits of understanding are commendable in his mouth.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 37:23.

A wise man instructeth his people; and the fruits of his understanding fail not.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 37:24.

A wise man shall be filled with blessing; and all they that see him shall count him happy.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 37:25.

The days of the life of man may be numbered: but the days of Israel are innumerable.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 37:26.

A wise man shall inherit glory among his people, and his name shall be perpetual.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 37:27.

My son, prove thy soul in thy life, and see what is evil for it, and give not that unto it.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 37:28.

For all things are not profitable for all men, neither hath every soul pleasure in every thing.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 37:29.

Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing, nor too greedy upon meats:

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 37:30.

For excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 37:31.

By surfeiting have many perished; but he that taketh heed prolongeth his life.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:1.

Honour a physician with the honour due unto him for the uses which ye may have of him: for the Lord hath created him.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:2.

For of the most High cometh healing, and he shall receive honour of the king.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:3.

The skill of the physician shall lift up his head: and in the sight of great men he shall be in admiration.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:4.

The Lord hath created medicines out of the earth; and he that is wise will not abhor them.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:5.

Was not the water made sweet with wood, that the virtue thereof might be known?

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:6.

And he hath given men skill, that he might be honoured in his marvellous works.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:7.

With such doth he heal [men], and taketh away their pains.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:8.

Of such doth the apothecary make a confection; and of his works there is no end; and from him is peace over all the earth,

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:9.

My son, in thy sickness be not negligent: but pray unto the Lord, and he will make thee whole.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:10.

Leave off from sin, and order thine hands aright, and cleanse thy heart from all wickedness.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:11.

Give a sweet savour, and a memorial of fine flour; and make a fat offering, as not being.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:12.

Then give place to the physician, for the Lord hath created him: let him not go from thee, for thou hast need of him.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:13.

There is a time when in their hands there is good success.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:14.

For they shall also pray unto the Lord, that he would prosper that, which they give for ease and remedy to prolong life.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:15.

He that sinneth before his Maker, let him fall into the hand of the physician.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:16.

My son, let tears fall down over the dead, and begin to lament, as if thou hadst suffered great harm thyself; and then cover his body according to the custom, and neglect not his burial.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:17.

Weep bitterly, and make great moan, and use lamentation, as he is worthy, and that a day or two, lest thou be evil spoken of: and then comfort thyself for thy heaviness.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:18.

For of heaviness cometh death, and the heaviness of the heart breaketh strength.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:19.

In affliction also sorrow remaineth: and the life of the poor is the curse of the heart.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:20.

Take no heaviness to heart: drive it away, and remember the last end.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:21.

Forget it not, for there is no turning again: thou shalt not do him good, but hurt thyself.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:22.

Remember my judgment: for thine also shall be so; yesterday for me, and to day for thee.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:23.

When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest; and be comforted for him, when his Spirit is departed from him.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:24.

The wisdom of a learned man cometh by opportunity of leisure: and he that hath little business shall become wise.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:25.

How can he get wisdom that holdeth the plough, and that glorieth in the goad, that driveth oxen, and is occupied in their labours, and whose talk is of bullocks?

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:26.

He giveth his mind to make furrows; and is diligent to give the kine fodder.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:27.

So every carpenter and workmaster, that laboureth night and day: and they that cut and grave seals, and are diligent to make great variety, and give themselves to counterfeit imagery, and watch to finish a work:

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:28.

The smith also sitting by the anvil, and considering the iron work, the vapour of the fire wasteth his flesh, and he fighteth with the heat of the furnace: the noise of the hammer and the anvil is ever in his ears, and his eyes look still upon the pattern of the thing that he maketh; he setteth his mind to finish his work, and watcheth to polish it perfectly:

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:29.

So doth the potter sitting at his work, and turning the wheel about with his feet, who is alway carefully set at his work, and maketh all his work by number;

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:30.

He fashioneth the clay with his arm, and boweth down his strength before his feet; he applieth himself to lead it over; and he is diligent to make clean the furnace:

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:31.

All these trust to their hands: and every one is wise in his work.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:32.

Without these cannot a city be inhabited: and they shall not dwell where they will, nor go up and down:

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:33.

They shall not be sought for in publick counsel, nor sit high in the congregation: they shall not sit on the judges’ seat, nor understand the sentence of judgment: they cannot declare justice and judgment; and they shall not be found where parables are spoken.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 38:34.

But they will maintain the state of the world, and [all] their desire is in the work of their craft.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:1.

But he that giveth his mind to the law of the most High, and is occupied in the meditation thereof, will seek out the wisdom of all the ancient, and be occupied in prophecies.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:2.

He will keep the sayings of the renowned men: and where subtil parables are, he will be there also.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:3.

He will seek out the secrets of grave sentences, and be conversant in dark parables.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:4.

He shall serve among great men, and appear before princes: he will travel through strange countries; for he hath tried the good and the evil among men.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:5.

He will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and will pray before the most High, and will open his mouth in prayer, and make supplication for his sins.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:6.

When the great Lord will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding: he shall pour out wise sentences, and give thanks unto the Lord in his prayer.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:7.

He shall direct his counsel and knowledge, and in his secrets shall he meditate.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:8.

He shall shew forth that which he hath learned, and shall glory in the law of the covenant of the Lord.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:9.

Many shall commend his understanding; and so long as the world endureth, it shall not be blotted out; his memorial shall not depart away, and his name shall live from generation to generation.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:10.

Nations shall shew forth his wisdom, and the congregation shall declare his praise.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:11.

If he die, he shall leave a greater name than a thousand: and if he live, he shall increase it.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:12.

Yet have I more to say, which I have thought upon; for I am filled as the moon at the full.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:13.

Hearken unto me, ye holy children, and bud forth as a rose growing by the brook of the field:

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:14.

And give ye a sweet savour as frankincense, and flourish as a lily, send forth a smell, and sing a song of praise, bless the Lord in all his works.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:15.

Magnify his name, and shew forth his praise with the songs of your lips, and with harps, and in praising him ye shall say after this manner:

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:16.

All the works of the Lord are exceeding good, and whatsoever he commandeth shall be accomplished in due season.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:17.

And none may say, What is this? wherefore is that? for at time convenient they shall all be sought out: at his commandment the waters stood as an heap, and at the words of his mouth the receptacles of waters.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:18.

At his commandment is done whatsoever pleaseth him; and none can hinder, when he will save.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:19.

The works of all flesh are before him, and nothing can be hid from his eyes.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:20.

He seeth from everlasting to everlasting; and there is nothing wonderful before him.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:21.

A man need not to say, What is this? wherefore is that? for he hath made all things for their uses.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:22.

His blessing covered the dry land as a river, and watered it as a flood.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:23.

As he hath turned the waters into saltness: so shall the heathen inherit his wrath.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:24.

As his ways are plain unto the holy; so are they stumblingblocks unto the wicked.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:25.

For the good are good things created from the beginning: so evil things for sinners.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:26.

The principal things for the whole use of man’s life are water, fire, iron, and salt, flour of wheat, honey, milk, and the blood of the grape, and oil, and clothing.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:27.

All these things are for good to the godly: so to the sinners they are turned into evil.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:28.

There be spirits that are created for vengeance, which in their fury lay on sore strokes; in the time of destruction they pour out their force, and appease the wrath of him that made them.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:29.

Fire, and hail, and famine, and death, all these were created for vengeance;

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:30.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:31.

They shall rejoice in his commandment, and they shall be ready upon earth, when need is; and when their time is come, they shall not transgress his word.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:32.

Therefore from the beginning I was resolved, and thought upon these things, and have left them in writing.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:33.

All the works of the Lord are good: and he will give every needful thing in due season.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:34.

So that a man cannot say, This is worse than that: for in time they shall all be well approved.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 39:35.

And therefore praise ye the Lord with the whole heart and mouth, and bless the name of the Lord.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:1.

Great travail is created for every man, and an heavy yoke is upon the sons of Adam, from the day that they go out of their mother’s womb, till the day that they return to the mother of all things.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:2.

Their imagination of things to come, and the day of death, [trouble] their thoughts, and [cause] fear of heart;

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:3.

From him that sitteth on a throne of glory, unto him that is humbled in earth and ashes;

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:4.

From him that weareth purple and a crown, unto him that is clothed with a linen frock.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:5.

Wrath, and envy, trouble, and unquietness, fear of death, and anger, and strife, and in the time of rest upon his bed his night sleep, do change his knowledge.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:6.

A little or nothing is his rest, and afterward he is in his sleep, as in a day of keeping watch, troubled in the vision of his heart, as if he were escaped out of a battle.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:7.

When all is safe, he awaketh, and marvelleth that the fear was nothing.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:8.

[Such things happen] unto all flesh, both man and beast, and that is sevenfold more upon sinners.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:9.

Death, and bloodshed, strife, and sword, calamities, famine, tribulation, and the scourge;

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:10.

These things are created for the wicked, and for their sakes came the flood.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:11.

All things that are of the earth shall turn to the earth again: and that which is of the waters doth return into the sea.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:12.

All bribery and injustice shall be blotted out: but true dealing shall endure for ever.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:13.

The goods of the unjust shall be dried up like a river, and shall vanish with noise, like a great thunder in rain.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:14.

While he openeth his hand he shall rejoice: so shall transgressors come to nought.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:15.

The children of the ungodly shall not bring forth many branches: but are as unclean roots upon a hard rock.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:16.

The weed growing upon every water and bank of a river shall be pulled up before all grass.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:17.

Bountifulness is as a most fruitful garden, and mercifulness endureth for ever.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:18.

To labour, and to be content with that a man hath, is a sweet life: but he that findeth a treasure is above them both.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:19.

Children and the building of a city continue a man’s name: but a blameless wife is counted above them both.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:20.

Wine and musick rejoice the heart: but the love of wisdom is above them both.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:21.

The pipe and the psaltery make sweet melody: but a pleasant tongue is above them both.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:22.

Thine eye desireth favour and beauty: but more than both corn while it is green.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:23.

A friend and companion never meet amiss: but above both is a wife with her husband.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:24.

Brethren and help are against time of trouble: but alms shall deliver more than them both.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:25.

Gold and silver make the foot stand sure: but counsel is esteemed above them both.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:26.

Riches and strength lift up the heart: but the fear of the Lord is above them both: there is no want in the fear of the Lord, and it needeth not to seek help.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:27.

The fear of the Lord is a fruitful garden, and covereth him above all glory.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:28.

My son, lead not a beggar’s life; for better it is to die than to beg.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:29.

The life of him that dependeth on another man’s table is not to be counted for a life; for he polluteth himself with other men’s meat: but a wise man well nurtured will beware thereof.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 40:30.

Begging is sweet in the mouth of the shameless: but in his belly there shall burn a fire.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:1.

O death, how bitter is the remembrance of thee to a man that liveth at rest in his possessions, unto the man that hath nothing to vex him, and that hath prosperity in all things: yea, unto him that is yet able to receive meat!

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:2.

O death, acceptable is thy sentence unto the needy, and unto him whose strength faileth, that is now in the last age, and is vexed with all things, and to him that despaireth, and hath lost patience!

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:3.

Fear not the sentence of death, remember them that have been before thee, and that come after; for this is the sentence of the Lord over all flesh.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:4.

And why art thou against the pleasure of the most High? there is no inquisition in the grave, whether thou have lived ten, or an hundred, or a thousand years.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:5.

The children of sinners are abominable children, and they that are conversant in the dwelling of the ungodly.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:6.

The inheritance of sinners’ children shall perish, and their posterity shall have a perpetual reproach.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:7.

The children will complain of an ungodly father, because they shall be reproached for his sake.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:8.

Woe be unto you, ungodly men, which have forsaken the law of the most high God! for if ye increase, it shall be to your destruction:

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:9.

And if ye be born, ye shall be born to a curse: and if ye die, a curse shall be your portion.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:10.

All that are of the earth shall turn to earth again: so the ungodly shall go from a curse to destruction.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:11.

The mourning of men is about their bodies: but an ill name of sinners shall be blotted out.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:12.

Have regard to thy name; for that shall continue with thee above a thousand great treasures of gold.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:13.

A good life hath but few days: but a good name endureth for ever.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:14.

My children, keep discipline in peace: for wisdom that is hid, and a treasure that is not seen, what profit is in them both?

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:15.

A man that hideth his foolishness is better than a man that hideth his wisdom.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:16.

Therefore be shamefaced according to my word: for it is not good to retain all shamefacedness; neither is it altogether approved in every thing.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:17.

Be ashamed of whoredom before father and mother: and of a lie before a prince and a mighty man;

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:18.

Of an offence before a judge and ruler; of iniquity before a congregation and people; of unjust dealing before thy partner and friend;

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:19.

And of theft in regard of the place where thou sojournest, and in regard of the truth of God and his covenant; and to lean with thine elbow upon the meat; and of scorning to give and take;

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:20.

And of silence before them that salute thee; and to look upon an harlot;

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:21.

And to turn away thy face from thy kinsman; or to take away a portion or a gift; or to gaze upon another man’s wife.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:22.

Or to be overbusy with his maid, and come not near her bed; or of upbraiding speeches before friends; and after thou hast given, upbraid not;

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:23.

Or of iterating and speaking again that which thou hast heard; and of revealing of secrets.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 41:24.

So shalt thou be truly shamefaced and find favour before all men.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:1.

Of these things be not thou ashamed, and accept no person to sin thereby:

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:2.

Of the law of the most High, and his covenant; and of judgment to justify the ungodly;

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:3.

Of reckoning with thy partners and travellers; or of the gift of the heritage of friends;

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:4.

Of exactness of balance and weights; or of getting much or little;

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:5.

And of merchants’ indifferent selling; of much correction of children; and to make the side of an evil servant to bleed.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:6.

Sure keeping is good, where an evil wife is; and shut up, where many hands are.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:7.

Deliver all things in number and weight; and put all in writing that thou givest out, or receivest in.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:8.

Be not ashamed to inform the unwise and foolish, and the extreme aged that contendeth with those that are young: thus shalt thou be truly learned, and approved of all men living.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:9.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:10.

In her virginity, lest she should be defiled and gotten with child in her father’s house; and having an husband, lest she should misbehave herself; and when she is married, lest she should be barren.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:11.

Keep a sure watch over a shameless daughter, lest she make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies, and a byword in the city, and a reproach among the people, and make thee ashamed before the multitude.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:12.

Behold not every body’s beauty, and sit not in the midst of women.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:13.

For from garments cometh a moth, and from women wickedness.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:14.

Better is the churlishness of a man than a courteous woman, a woman, I say, which bringeth shame and reproach.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:15.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:16.

The sun that giveth light looketh upon all things, and the work thereof is full of the glory of the Lord.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:17.

The Lord hath not given power to the saints to declare all his marvellous works, which the Almighty Lord firmly settled, that whatsoever is might be established for his glory.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:18.

He seeketh out the deep, and the heart, and considereth their crafty devices: for the Lord knoweth all that may be known, and he beholdeth the signs of the world.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:19.

He declareth the things that are past, and for to come, and revealeth the steps of hidden things.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:20.

No thought escapeth him, neither any word is hidden from him.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:21.

He hath garnished the excellent works of his wisdom, and he is from everlasting to everlasting: unto him may nothing be added, neither can he be diminished, and he hath no need of any counsellor.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:22.

Oh how desirable are all his works! and that a man may see even to a spark.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:23.

All these things live and remain for ever for all uses, and they are all obedient.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:24.

All things are double one against another: and he hath made nothing imperfect.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 42:25.

One thing establisheth the good or another: and who shall be filled with beholding his glory?

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:1.

The pride of the height, the clear firmament, the beauty of heaven, with his glorious shew;

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:2.

The sun when it appeareth, declaring at his rising a marvellous instrument, the work of the most High:

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:3.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:4.

A man blowing a furnace is in works of heat, but the sun burneth the mountains three times more; breathing out fiery vapours, and sending forth bright beams, it dimmeth the eyes.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:5.

Great is the Lord that made it; and at his commandment runneth hastily.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:6.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:7.

From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:8.

The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her changing, being an instrument of the armies above, shining in the firmament of heaven;

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:9.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:10.

At the commandment of the Holy One they will stand in their order, and never faint in their watches.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:11.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:12.

It compasseth the heaven about with a glorious circle, and the hands of the most High have bended it.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:13.

By his commandment he maketh the snow to fall aplace, and sendeth swiftly the lightnings of his judgment.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:14.

Through this the treasures are opened: and clouds fly forth as fowls.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:15.

By his great power he maketh the clouds firm, and the hailstones are broken small.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:16.

At his sight the mountains are shaken, and at his will the south wind bloweth.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:17.

The noise of the thunder maketh the earth to tremble: so doth the northern storm and the whirlwind: as birds flying he scattereth the snow, and the falling down thereof is as the lighting of grasshoppers:

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:18.

The eye marvelleth at the beauty of the whiteness thereof, and the heart is astonished at the raining of it.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:19.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:20.

When the cold north wind bloweth, and the water is congealed into ice, it abideth upon every gathering together of water, and clotheth the water as with a breastplate.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:21.

It devoureth the mountains, and burneth the wilderness, and consumeth the grass as fire.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:22.

A present remedy of all is a mist coming speedily, a dew coming after heat refresheth.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:23.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:24.

They that sail on the sea tell of the danger thereof; and when we hear it with our ears, we marvel thereat.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:25.

For therein be strange and wondrous works, variety of all kinds of beasts and whales created.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:26.

By him the end of them hath prosperous success, and by his word all things consist.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:27.

We may speak much, and yet come short: wherefore in sum, he is all.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:28.

How shall we be able to magnify him? for he is great above all his works.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:29.

The Lord is terrible and very great, and marvellous is his power.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:30.

When ye glorify the Lord, exalt him as much as ye can; for even yet will he far exceed: and when ye exalt him, put forth all your strength, and be not weary; for ye can never go far enough.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:31.

Who hath seen him, that he might tell us? and who can magnify him as he is?

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:32.

There are yet hid greater things than these be, for we have seen but a few of his works.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 43:33.

For the Lord hath made all things; and to the godly hath he given wisdom.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:1.

Let us now praise famous men, and our fathers that begat us.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:2.

The Lord hath wrought great glory by them through his great power from the beginning.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:3.

Such as did bear rule in their kingdoms, men renowned for their power, giving counsel by their understanding, and declaring prophecies:

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:4.

Leaders of the people by their counsels, and by their knowledge of learning meet for the people, wise and eloquent are their instructions:

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:5.

Such as found out musical tunes, and recited verses in writing:

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:6.

Rich men furnished with ability, living peaceably in their habitations:

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:7.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:8.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:9.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:10.

But these were merciful men, whose righteousness hath not been forgotten.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:11.

With their seed shall continually remain a good inheritance, and their children are within the covenant.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:12.

Their seed standeth fast, and their children for their sakes.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:13.

Their seed shall remain for ever, and their glory shall not be blotted out.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:14.

Their bodies are buried in peace; but their name liveth for evermore.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:15.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:16.

Enoch pleased the Lord, and was translated, being an example of repentance to all generations.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:17.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:18.

An everlasting covenant was made with him, that all flesh should perish no more by the flood.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:19.

Abraham was a great father of many people: in glory was there none like unto him;

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:20.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:21.

Therefore he assured him by an oath, that he would bless the nations in his seed, and that he would multiply him as the dust of the earth, and exalt his seed as the stars, and cause them to inherit from sea to sea, and from the river unto the utmost part of the land.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:22.

With Isaac did he establish likewise [for Abraham his father’s sake] the blessing of all men, and the covenant,

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 44:23.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 45:1.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 45:2.

He made him like to the glorious saints, and magnified him, so that his enemies stood in fear of him.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 45:3.

By his words he caused the wonders to cease, and he made him glorious in the sight of kings, and gave him a commandment for his people, and shewed him part of his glory.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 45:4.

He sanctified him in his faithfuless and meekness, and chose him out of all men.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 45:5.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 45:6.

He exalted Aaron, an holy man like unto him, even his brother, of the tribe of Levi.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 45:7.

An everlasting covenant he made with him and gave him the priesthood among the people; he beautified him with comely ornaments, and clothed him with a robe of glory.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 45:8.

He put upon him perfect glory; and strengthened him with rich garments, with breeches, with a long robe, and the ephod.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 45:9.

And he compassed him with pomegranates, and with many golden bells round about, that as he went there might be a sound, and a noise made that might be heard in the temple, for a memorial to the children of his people;

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 45:10.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 45:11.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 45:13.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 45:14.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 45:15.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 45:16.

I prayed for her before the temple, and will seek her out even to the end.

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 51:15.

Even from the flower till the grape was ripe hath my heart delighted in her: my foot went the right way, from my youth up sought I after her.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 51:16.

I bowed down mine ear a little, and received her, and gat much learning.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 51:17.

I profited therein, therefore will I ascribe glory unto him that giveth me wisdom.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 51:18.

For I purposed to do after her, and earnestly I followed that which is good; so shall I not be confounded.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 51:19.

My soul hath wrestled with her, and in my doings I was exact: I stretched forth my hands to the heaven above, and bewailed my ignorances of her.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 51:20.

I directed my soul unto her, and I found her in pureness: I have had my heart joined with her from the beginning, therefore shall I not be foresaken.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 51:21.

My heart was troubled in seeking her: therefore have I gotten a good possession.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 51:22.

The Lord hath given me a tongue for my reward, and I will praise him therewith.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 51:23.

Draw near unto me, ye unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 51:24.

Wherefore are ye slow, and what say ye to these things, seeing your souls are very thirsty?

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 51:25.

I opened my mouth, and said, Buy her for yourselves without money.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 51:26.

Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction: she is hard at hand to find.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 51:27.

Behold with your eyes, how that I have but little labour, and have gotten unto me much rest.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 51:28.

Get learning with a great sum of money, and get much gold by her.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 51:29.

Let your soul rejoice in his mercy, and be not ashamed of his praise.

↩

The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus 51:30.

Work your work betimes, and in his time he will give you your reward.
